UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the PDF Spark application, linking to an external authentication system. This entity stores non-sensitive, application-specific user data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This ID is typically provided by and linked to an external authentication system.

displayName.description: An optional display name for the user, used for personalization within the application interface.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was first created in the PDF Spark application.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the user profile was updated.

File.title: File
File.description: Represents a document file (e.g., PDF, Word, Image) either uploaded by a user or generated as an output of a processing job.

id.description: Unique identifier for the File entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity that owns or is associated with this file. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N File)

originalFileName.description: The original name of the file as provided by the user during upload.

storedFileName.description: The unique name given to the file when stored in the underlying storage system (e.g., a UUID).

fileExtension.description: The file extension of the document (e.g., 'pdf', 'docx', 'jpg').

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/jpeg').

sizeBytes.description: The size of the file in bytes.

storageReference.description: A reference or path (e.g., S3 object key, internal path) to the file's physical location in the storage system.

uploadedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the file was uploaded or created.

status.description: The current lifecycle status of the file (e.g., 'uploaded', 'processing', 'available', 'deleted').

expiresAt.description: Optional timestamp indicating when a temporary file is scheduled for automatic deletion.

ProcessingJob.title: ProcessingJob
ProcessingJob.description: Represents a single PDF processing operation (such as merge, split, convert, or AI analysis) initiated by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ProcessingJob entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity that initiated this processing job. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ProcessingJob)

jobType.description: The specific type of PDF operation performed (e.g., 'MergePDF', 'SplitPDF', 'ConvertPDFToWord', 'AnalyzePDF').

status.description: The current status of the processing job (e.g., 'Pending', 'Processing', 'Completed', 'Failed', 'Cancelled').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the processing job was initially created.

startedAt.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the processing job began execution.

completedAt.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the processing job successfully completed or failed.

errorMessage.description: Contains a descriptive error message if the processing job failed.

configuration.description: A JSON string containing job-specific parameters, such as page ranges for splitting, target format for conversion, or AI analysis prompts/models.

inputFileIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the File entities that were used as input for this job. (Relationship: ProcessingJob N:N File)

outputFileIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the File entities that were generated as output by this job. (Relationship: ProcessingJob N:N File)

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The document ID (`{userId}`) must match the `id` field within the document and the authenticated user's UID (`request.auth.uid`). This structure enables direct, path-based authorization for user data.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching `request.auth.uid` and the UserProfile's `id`.

definition.description: Stores metadata for files uploaded or generated by a specific user. The `{userId}` in the path must match `request.auth.uid` and the `userId` field within the File document. The `{fileId}` is the unique identifier for the file document. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this file, matching `request.auth.uid` and the 'userId' field in the document.

params.name: fileId
params.description: The unique identifier for the file document.

definition.description: Stores details for processing jobs initiated by a specific user. The `{userId}` in the path must match `request.auth.uid` and the `userId` field within the ProcessingJob document. The `{jobId}` is the unique identifier for the job document. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who initiated this job, matching `request.auth.uid` and the 'userId' field in the document.

params.name: jobId
params.description: The unique identifier for the processing job document.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for PDF Spark prioritizes Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and clear Access Modeling to ensure robust security and debuggability. All user-specific data, including profiles, uploaded files, and initiated processing jobs, is organized hierarchically under a user's unique ID. This approach places the primary authorization context directly within the document path, simplifying security rules and enhancing performance.

1.  **Authorization Independence (Denormalization):**
    *   `UserProfile` documents are stored at `/users/{userId}`. The document ID (`userId`) itself serves as the authorization context. Access to this document directly depends on `request.auth.uid` matching the `{userId}` wildcard.
    *   For `File` documents (at `/users/{userId}/files/{fileId}`) and `ProcessingJob` documents (at `/users/{userId}/jobs/{jobId}`), the `userId` is present in the parent path wildcard `{userId}`. Crucially, each `File` and `ProcessingJob` document also contains a `userId` field within its data (`resource.data.userId`). For Authorization Independence, this `resource.data.userId` MUST match the path's `{userId}` (and `request.auth.uid`). This explicit denormalization eliminates the need for `get()` calls to parent documents in security rules, ensuring atomic operations and preventing complex, hard-to-debug rule dependencies. For example, a rule for files would check `if request.auth.uid == userId && resource.data.userId == userId;`.

2.  **Structural Segregation & QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
    *   **User Profiles:** `/users/{userId}` ensures each user's profile is a distinct, path-secured entity. List operations on `/users` would typically be disallowed or limited to only the requesting user's profile, adhering to QAPs.
    *   **User Files:** `/users/{userId}/files/{fileId}` segregates files by owner. This path design naturally supports Query-Aware Permissions (QAPs). When a user queries their own files (e.g., `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('files').get()`), the security rules can efficiently verify `request.auth.uid == userId` for the path segment, ensuring only files belonging to the authenticated user are returned. This prevents clients from inadvertently or maliciously listing files owned by other users.
    *   **Processing Jobs:** Similarly, `/users/{userId}/jobs/{jobId}` isolates processing jobs to their respective owners. QAPs are satisfied as listing operations are confined to the authenticated user's jobs, verified by the path-based `userId` wildcard.

This design leverages explicit ownership in path structures and denormalized `userId` fields within documents to create a clear, secure, and performant data model that simplifies Firestore security rules and inherently supports QAP requirements.
